s1.syndrome_frame: Acute inflammatory arthritis following intra-articular injection
salient_findings: Acute bilateral knee swelling and pain
Elevated peripheral white blood cell count and inflammatory markers
key_facts: 61-year-old African American woman
Bilateral knee osteoarthritis
Third weekly Synvisc viscosupplementation injections in each knee
Onset of pain 12 hours after injections
No fever, chills, or malaise
Right knee: suprapatellar effusion, range of motion 0-70°, no erythema, no pain with micromotion
Left knee: moderate suprapatellar effusion, range of motion 0-30°, no erythema, pain with micromotion
Peripheral white blood cell count of 12.8×10^3/mm³
C-reactive protein level of 159 mg/L
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 79 mm/hr
Bilateral knee arthrocentesis with elevated synovial fluid WBC count
Negative gram stain and cultures in both knees

differentials: Infectious arthritis due to atypical bacteria
per_call: Infectious arthritis due to atypical bacteria

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of pain and swelling after intra-articular injection, elevated synovial fluid WBC count

shortlist.label: Viscosupplementation-related inflammatory reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Recent Synvisc viscosupplementation injections, negative cultures and gram stain

shortlist.label: Crystal-induced arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute inflammatory arthritis, elevated peripheral white blood cell count and C-reactive protein level

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity reaction to Synvisc
shortlist.why_kept: Onset of pain 12 hours after Synvisc injections, absence of fever, chills, or malaise

shortlist.label: Gonococcal arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of pain and swelling, negative cultures and gram stain, but possibility of atypical bacteria

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute bilateral knee swelling and pain after receiving Synvisc viscosupplementation injections, with elevated synovial fluid WBC counts but negative gram stains and cultures, suggesting a non-infectious inflammatory reaction to the injections.

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: Negative gram stains and cultures in both knees make infection unlikely

rejected.label: Crystal-induced arthritis
rejected.why: No mention of crystal analysis or characteristic joint findings

rejected.label: Hypersensitivity reaction to Synvisc
rejected.why: The presentation is more consistent with a localized inflammatory reaction rather than a systemic hypersensitivity reaction

rejected.label: Gonococcal arthritis
rejected.why: No mention of systemic symptoms or risk factors for gonococcal infection
